questions.prompt: What does "exemplary product" mean for CustomReport?
questions.description: The proposed definition keeps the product outcome primary and treats environment work only as supporting proof.
questions.recommendedAnswer: A coherent architecture; explicit, enforced code-style rules for formatting, naming, module boundaries, public APIs, duplication and suppressions; maintainable, safe code; complete user-facing flows with accessible, responsive UX; deterministic automated tests and live product proof; operationally observable and recoverable delivery; and documentation that enables the team to change the product safely.

questions.prompt: How should runtime and infrastructure work be constrained?
questions.description: This decides whether environment activity is an end in itself or only evidence for product quality.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Use only the minimal isolated runtime, CI and observability work needed to prove product behavior, resilience and release readiness. Do not pursue standalone environment optimization unless it blocks a product-quality requirement.

questions.prompt: What must be true before we call the goal complete?
questions.description: The recommended bar prevents local green checks or historical evidence from substituting for product readiness.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Every active product requirement and accepted OpenSpec change is reconciled; no blocking architecture, code-quality, functional, accessibility, data-integrity, observability or recovery finding remains; targeted and full required checks pass; fresh source-bound live evidence covers the applicable product denominator; release/CI evidence is current; and an independent final review passes.

options.label: Fresh live evidence covers the product
